cohort: 835 mother-infant pairs from the Barwon Infant Study
finding: Maternal GBS colonization and intrapartum antibiotic use were associated with increased infant aIMT in vaginal deliveries, while antenatal pet exposure was associated with decreased aIMT in vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Maternal GBS colonization and intrapartum antibiotics were associated with increased infant aIMT in those delivered vaginally, whereas antenatal pet exposure was associated with decreased aIMT in those delivered vaginally.
birth_weight: Measured, but specific values not provided
